newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks record eighth straight win.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks record eighth straight win.

text.p: Argentine stocks erased early losses to close higher for the eighth session running Monday, bucking the trend on Wall Street.
But bidding slowed to less than half Friday's volume and prices were seen hovering sideways short-term, dealers said.

"The market is moving on technical factors, trying to consolidate," said Emilio Alessandro. "Selective buying offset profit-taking today, and we're likely to see the same kind of mixed bag in the next few days."
The MerVal index .MERV inched up 0.2 percent to 579.06. It had jumped 6.1 percent in the previous seven sessions.
Floor volume dwindled to 10.8 million pesos from 24 million Friday, while over-the-counter volume shrank to 110.1 million pesos from 175 million Friday.
The broad market index matched MerVal gains of 0.2 percent, with winners and losers tied at 22 and 16 issues closing flat.

"Many players will see this lull as a buying opportunity, especially if the (U.S.) long bond yield ticks higher and heads off a relatively strong correction here," said one analyst at a U.S.-based investment bank. "But for now it seems the market has just lost its momentum."

Stocks have risen in the past several weeks on a series of domestic cues, including tax hikes, planned labor and health care reforms, the placement of a $1.0 billion global bond, improving economic indicators such as industrial production and trade data, and preliminary International Monetary Fund approval of new fiscal targets.
But analysts note stocks have largely underperformed bonds and have room to stretch.
The day's top MerVal performers were carmaker Sevel, steelmaker Acindar and Bansud bank, which jumped 4.5 percent, 3.2 percent and 2.6 percent, respectively.

Oil giant YPF, the market bellwether, also posted a hefty gain of 1.5 percent. London's Latinvest brokers said early Monday the stock was undervalued against its rivals and forecast that YPF would be a major beneficiary of long-term oil price increases.
Heaviest main-tier losses were in petrochemical concern Ipako, steelmaker Siderar and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which slid 4.0 percent, 3.7 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
